purpose: Every place this estate records work that is not finished, declared in one file so that npm run outstanding can total them. Until 2026-09-14 there were five such places and no command that knew about more than two: npm run readiness counted 48 items, npm run commission counted those plus the governance findings, and the other three were counted by nothing. A question as ordinary as 'how much is left' had no answer, and each source read as if it were the whole picture.
whyFederatedRatherThanMerged: Merging them was the obvious move and it is the wrong one. The governance findings gate no pilot key, so folding them into a register whose every other row does would misrepresent both. The two audits are records — this estate does not rewrite a record to make it a task list, for the same reason docs/audits/ is exempt from every claim gate. And the pending-work register belongs to a workstream with its own owner. What was missing was never one register; it was one TOTAL. A source may keep its own shape, its own lifecycle and its own owner, and still be counted.
howToAddOne: Add an entry here. tests/outstanding-sources.test.mjs fails when a register-shaped document exists under docs/ and is not declared, so a new register cannot quietly become a sixth place nobody counts.

sources.title: Production readiness register
sources.authority: The register of record for commissioning. ACTION_PLAN.md, EXECUTION_RUNBOOK.md and IMPLEMENTATION_WALKTHROUGH.md are generated from it; npm run test:closure holds every document and npm run commission itself to it.

sources.title: Governance estate position
sources.authority: The ten SharePoint lists that carry identity, RBAC and audit. Kept separate because the endpoint commissioning path does not touch them today — but the seven internal designer-paste packages that will serve the pilot keys all read DGO_UserDirectory and DGO_RoleCatalogue, so that separation is a fact about the currently deployed flows, not a permanent property.

sources.title: Notification tenant-execution pending work
sources.allOpenBecause: The document carries no status convention, and its own preamble states the position for every entry: 'Repository implementation is complete. The work below requires tenant access, institutional decisions, operational evidence or approval.' Counting them all open is what the document says, not an assumption about it.
sources.authority: The notification workstream's own list. Referenced by one prose sentence in closure-disposition.json and by nothing else, which is why it was invisible.

sources.title: Notification estate full-scope assessment, 2026-09-09
sources.allOpenBecause: An audit is a record of what was true on its date and is never edited to agree with the present — the rule docs/audits/ already lives by. So nothing in it can be marked closed in place. Its findings are counted as outstanding until an item in another source supersedes them, and none does yet. F-02 records a partial correction inline and its governance half is stated as open.
sources.authority: A record, not a task list. It is counted here because its ten findings are real outstanding work that appears in no register, not because the file should become one. Ten, not the nine a hand count first reported — F-10 sits below the visible run of F-01 to F-09, which is the ordinary way a hand count goes wrong and the reason this one is read by a pattern.

sources.title: Flow-truth persistence review
sources.allOpenBecause: A record is not edited to agree with the present, so no finding is ever closed in place. Until 2026-09-15 that meant all 29 stayed counted open: the rebuilt DGO_FLOW_TRUTH_PERSISTENCE package answered most of them, but tests/flow-truth-persistence.test.mjs asserted no finding by id, so nothing established WHICH. Something does now — see supersededBy. The default is still open; a finding leaves it only when the declaration names the assertion that answers it.

supersededBy.because: The rebuilt package is held to this finding by a named assertion in tests/flow-truth-persistence.test.mjs, which fails if the defect returns.
supersededBy.note: This supersedes the PACKAGE defect each finding raises. It resolves nothing in the tenant: B1's three lists still do not exist, and the assertion that covers B1 is precisely that the package says so rather than pretending otherwise. tests/flow-truth-coverage.test.mjs holds the declaration to both documents it spans — every finding in the review is declared, and every assertion cited exists in the suite.

sources.authority: A record. Includes two security findings, S1 and S2, which is why leaving them uncounted mattered.
sources.note: The pattern allows a range head — C11–C12 covers two findings under one heading, and counting it once would under-report by one.

sources.notCountedBecause: A record of the merge that produced this baseline. Its R- ids are recommendations about that merge, which has happened.

sources.title: Design audit brief assessment
sources.notCountedBecause: Its live remnant is ITEM-57 in the readiness register — the archived design system, unreconciled, a decision for the agency. Counted there.

sources.title: Repository hygiene, phase 3 findings
sources.notCountedBecause: Assessed against commit c2d78ba2ea23 at 294 tracked files; this tree has 1,900. A record of a scope that no longer exists.

sources.title: Closure register
sources.notCountedBecause: Generated from the readiness register and the governance estate position, and it lists only what those two record as CLOSED. Counting it would double every discharged item and, worse, count closed work as outstanding — the exact inversion this estate spent a week correcting. It is register-shaped by construction, which is why it is declared here rather than exempted silently.

sources.title: Master register
sources.notCountedBecause: Generated from every counted source in this file — it enumerates the same open items with what each one needs to close, and carries no item of its own. Counting it would double all 87. It is the most register-shaped document in the estate, which is exactly why it is declared rather than exempted: a document that reads as the master list is the most dangerous place for an uncounted item to appear.

whyUncountedSourcesAreStillDeclared: A document can be register-shaped and still not be a place work hides — because it RESTATES a counted source, or because it is a record whose live findings have since been taken up elsewhere. Those are declared here with counted:false and the reason, rather than left out. Leaving them out would mean the declaration could not be checked against the repository, and a silent exemption list is how a sixth register eventually appears: somebody adds a file, the gate is quiet, and nobody ever decides. Declared-and-uncounted is a decision on the record. npm run outstanding prints them so the judgement can be disagreed with.
